name: fixed-point nesting effect

phase_0.boundary_condition: The recursive container where the outer operator acts on the inner object, enforcing the condition that closure occurs if and only if the inner object is a fixed point of the outer action.

⊢.justification: The uninitialized state before the nesting operation is defined, representing the raw distance ||B(A)-A|| before classification.

⊣.justification: The terminal anchor defining the scope of the nesting operation, where the outer operator B contains the inner object A.

≻.justification: The forward morphism representing the iterative descent of an object within the basin of attraction toward the fixed point.

≺.justification: The reverse morphism representing the evaluation of the residual ||B(A)-A|| to determine if the object is already at the fixed point.

⋈.justification: The sequential chaining of the outer operator B acting on the inner object A, forming the composite B(A).

⊙.justification: The identity state where the inner object A recognizes itself as the fixed point of B, satisfying B(A)=A.

∈.justification: The split into three exhaustive classes: one-shot (fixed point), iterated (basin), and no-closure (outside basin).

∋.justification: The reconstitution of the classification arms into a single verdict regarding the closure status of the nesting.

⊤.justification: The affirmative state where the residual is zero and the nesting closes in one shot.

⊥.justification: The negative state where the object is outside the basin and no fixed point is reachable.

⊞.justification: The state holding both the current position and the target fixed point simultaneously during the iterative convergence process.

⊡.justification: The permanent record of the integer winding number that prevents continuous deformation to a trivial state.

phase_2.failure_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.void_description: The state before the nesting is defined, where the residual ||B(A)-A|| is undefined and no classification exists.
phase_3.true_description: The state where the inner object is a fixed point of the outer operator, resulting in one-shot closure with zero iterations.
phase_3.false_description: The state where the inner object is outside the basin of attraction, resulting in no closure and a persistent seam.
phase_3.both_description: The state where the inner object is in the basin but not yet at the fixed point, holding the current position and the target simultaneously during iteration.

steps.domain_action: Initialize the pre-nest residual state before any nesting operation is defined.
Fork the classification into three exhaustive classes based on the residual ||B(A)-A||.
Traverse the basin of attraction for objects not yet at the fixed point.
Affirm the one-shot closure state where the residual is zero and B(A)=A.
Chain the outer operator B acting on the inner object A to form the composite.
Establish the self-model where the inner object recognizes itself as the fixed point.
Hold the paradice state of simultaneous current position and target during iterative convergence.
Reverse to check the residual and determine if the object is already at the fixed point.
Affirm the no-closure state where the object is outside the basin and no fixed point is reachable.
Record the integer winding number that prevents continuous deformation to a trivial state.
Fuse the classification arms into a single verdict regarding the closure status.
Compose the verified closure state with the outer operator's action.
Re-establish the identity of the closed system where the boundary encodes the interior state.
Anchor the system at the closure boundary where the nesting is complete.

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The residual predictor that translates the pre-nest distance ||B(A)-A|| into a classification of one-shot, iterated, or no-closure.
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: The Frobenius structure μ∘δ=id that communicates the fixed-point status between the inner object and the outer operator.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The holographic state V=L(x) where the boundary encodes the entire interior state of the nesting.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The operator kind (dissipative vs conservative) that determines which classes populate the classification fork.
phase_5.alfs_store: The d=12 SIC fiducial as the canonical reference for one-shot closure under the Zauner action.

phase_6.cycle_cost: The computational budget set by the starting distance from the fixed point for iterated closure.
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: The state where the inner object is either at the fixed point, in the basin, or outside the basin.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: The state where the nesting has either closed in one shot, converged iteratively, or failed to close.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The nesting operation is entropy-conservative because the residual predictor classifies the outcome without consuming additional information, and the closure is determined by the structural properties of the operator and object.
